dialect.detail: GnuCOBOL (OpenCOBOL) targeting Brazilian SPED/ECD (Escrituração Contábil Digital) electronic accounting export; uses *> inline comments, VALUE x'7C', z-string literals, and DECIMAL-POINT IS COMMA — all GnuCOBOL/OpenCOBOL idioms; developed by pBranaSoftware.com

purpose.domain_detail: Brazilian SPED ECD (Escrituração Contábil Digital / Livro de Escrituração Contábil Digital) — mandatory electronic accounting bookkeeping export for Brazilian federal tax authority (Receita Federal)
purpose.summary: CT900 generates the electronic accounting export file (ECD/LECD) required by the Brazilian SPED system. It reads from multiple accounting data files (chart of accounts, cost centers, ledger entries, balances, etc.) and writes pipe-delimited records conforming to the LECD layout specification. The program handles company identification (CNPJ, state registration), account plans, journal entries, and balance records.

notable_features: 44 COPY statements for modular file definitions
REDEFINES used extensively for numeric/alphanumeric dual access
Pipe-delimited output format for SPED ECD
No COMP-3 usage despite financial application
verdict.notes: Source truncated to first 16000 chars; full file is ~225KB/5147 lines. Program is clearly a real production accounting export utility for Brazilian regulatory compliance. GnuCOBOL dialect confirmed by *> comments and z-string literals. No COMP-3 is unusual for financial COBOL but consistent with GnuCOBOL practice on this platform.
